Text: Descriptive naming improves codebase maintainability by choosing intent-revealing names to prevent {{c1::cognitive overload}} during development.
Extra: Obscure variable names require constant lookups and mental tracking. Clean names explain themselves, saving developer time.

Text: Primitive and String public static final constants are optimized at compile-time via {{c1::constant inlining}} by the Java compiler.
Extra: The javac compiler inserts the literal constant value directly into the consuming class's bytecode, avoiding runtime getstatic lookup instructions.

Text: The guard-clause pattern relies on early returns or throwing exceptions to maintain a {{c1::flat control flow}} structure in methods.
Extra: Rather than nesting business logic inside nested if-else statements, guard clauses handle invalid parameters first, keeping the happy path linear.

Text: Swallowing exceptions by using empty catch blocks breaks the JVM's stack-unwinding mechanism and discards the {{c1::diagnostic context}} of the error.
Extra: Halting the exception propagation without logging or wrapping it hides developer bugs and leaves the system in an unstable state.

Text: Custom exceptions should extend {{c1::RuntimeException}} if they represent unrecoverable programmer errors that callers cannot resolve.
Extra: Extending RuntimeException creates an unchecked exception, which does not require compile-time throws clauses or try-catch blocks.

Text: Custom exceptions should extend {{c1::Exception}} if they represent recoverable business conditions that the caller must handle.
Extra: Checked exceptions are verified at compile-time. The compiler requires callers to handle them or declare them in their method signature.

Text: The strict contract states that if two objects are equal under equals(), they must return the {{c1::same hashCode}} value.
Extra: If they do not, hash-based collections like HashMap and HashSet will fail to retrieve or store the objects correctly.

Text: To avoid heap allocations and $O(N^2)$ time complexity, loop string concatenation should use {{c1::StringBuilder}} instead of the `+` operator.
Extra: Strings are immutable in Java. Every plus operator concatenation in a loop generates a new String instance on the heap.

Text: For monetary arithmetic, Java developers should use {{c1::BigDecimal}} with its String constructor to prevent IEEE 754 floating-point rounding errors.
Extra: Primitives like double and float represent numbers in binary scientific notation, which cannot represent base-10 fractions (like 0.1) exactly.

Text: The try-with-resources statement automatically closes resources that implement the {{c1::AutoCloseable}} interface.
Extra: This guarantees that system resources such as file handles and sockets are safely closed even if runtime exceptions occur.

Text: Composition is preferred over class inheritance because it avoids the {{c1::Fragile Base Class}} coupling problem.
Extra: Inheritance creates a tight compile-time link between subclasses and parent classes. Changes in parent methods can break subclasses.

Text: Using raw types instead of generic parameterized collections disables {{c1::compile-time type safety}} checking.
Extra: Raw types are generic types used without type parameters. They cause compiler warnings and risk runtime ClassCastExceptions.
